name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+22 partisan lean makes a Democratic win structurally improbable
Bost holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage with $846K on hand versus Fortier's $34K
Prediction markets price Bost near 98 percent to win
No public polling or expert ratings indicate the race is competitive
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Bost's overwhelming fundraising edge, and prediction markets pricing him near 98 percent all point the same direction, and no polling or outside spending suggests any countervailing force. Fortier's modest war chest leaves little path to closing a margin this wide.
model.watch: A major scandal, a sharp national shift toward Democrats, or surprise polling showing a single-digit race would be the main reasons to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southern Illinois's 12th District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Mike Bost returns as the strong favorite after clearing his primary. The district's partisan baseline of roughly R+22 sets a high bar for any challenger, and no general-election polling has emerged to suggest the race is competitive. Prediction markets put Bost's chances near 98 percent.

Julie Fortier has raised about $159,000 with modest cash on hand, while Bost has built a war chest of roughly $846,000 from $1.6 million raised, with no significant outside spending on either side. The fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing all align, making an upset highly unlikely barring an unexpected shift in the political environment.
